content.thinking:
I need to write the whole file in a single pass since I can't test incrementally, so I'll stick to well-understood API calls like part with multiple geometries, tileBox, rod, extrude, lathe, pixel textures, and cellPaint. I'm checking how existing samples structure their builder creation and exports, then planning out a dungeon prop group on a flagstone floor as the design concept.

I'm sketching the scene: barrels, crate stacks, a wooden table with candle, an open treasure chest, a standing brazier with fire glow, a stone pillar fragment, a weapon rack with swords, a skull pile, cobwebs, sacks, and potion bottles — keeping it rich but manageable, all floor-standing props with no base plinth. I'm setting a small texel size and planning tile textures for planks, stone, and metal, plus a helper function for building boxes with tinted textures. For the barrel I'm defining a lathe profile to shape the rounded wooden form.

Now I'm adding hoop rings around the barrel using thin lathe rings that follow the barrel's radius at each height, and I'm figuring out a piecewise linear function to interpolate that radius. For the brazier, I'm building a lathe bowl with leg rods and crossing textured planes to fake a glowing flame effect.

For the chest, I'm building the body as a tiled box and the curved lid as an extruded semicircular profile, placing it centered above the base and adding gold band details along the surface.

I decide to keep the chest closed with a lock, adding a small pile of coins nearby as flat cylinders rather than attempting a complex open-lid tilt. For the skull pile, I'm thinking through how to build a pixelated skull using boxes for the cranium and jaw, with a custom skin layout that paints eye sockets, nose, and teeth onto the front face.

Bones can be simple rods with box knobs on the ends. For the weapon rack, I'm planning posts and a crossbar holding a sword, axe, and spear, each built from flat boxes for blades and extruded shapes for the axe head. I'm also laying out a table scene with candles, books, and potions resting on a tiled tabletop with four legs.

Adding stone rubble for a broken pillar, a simple web texture on crossed planes for cobwebs, crate stacks with plank and strap details, and squished-sphere sacks tied at the top to round out the scene layout.

Adjusting rack height to 1.3 and placing the table, chest, brazier, and skull pile cluster near the back, with sacks tucked beside the table, making sure every item's base sits flush at floor level with no awkward overlaps.

Now I'm setting up the builder and RNG seed, then defining the wood plank texture using a color ramp with seam lines, highlights, and grain variation drawn per row using hashed randomness for a pixel-dungeon look.

Writing stone brick texture...

I need a metal strap texture with rivets, then a helper function that wraps tiled box geometry with texture, randomization, and optional rotation into a reusable part builder.

I'm planning the crate's construction: a plank cube body, darker corner posts, metal straps top and bottom, and a diagonal brace made from a thin rotated plank box crossing the front face at roughly 40 degrees, sized to span the diagonal without clipping too far past the edges.

Now I'm working out how to rotate the whole crate prop around its Y axis by composing a helper function that transforms local coordinates into world positions using rotation math, so each box part can be placed correctly whether it's a straight panel or the angled diagonal brace.

For barrels, I'm computing stave divisions around the round surface by angle, shading each stave with a wood palette ramp plus noise, with darker shading on the rim and inner top face, and a separate iron color for the hoops with a highlight.

I'm settling on 10 faceted segments for the barrel for that pixel-faceted look. For the lathe parameters, I'm handling the top lid as a slightly smaller recessed cylinder with a flat dark wood color, skipping plank texture detail for simplicity.

Now I'm working out the brazier's bowl profile as a lathe shape, making sure the outer and inner wall points don't cross so the geometry stays consistent, then moving on to adding three supporting legs connecting down from the bowl.

Writing flame texture rows...

Finishing the flame pixel pattern with orange and yellow tones, then sketching a small glowing torch part using the glow helper, and starting to lay out scene positions for a pillar and crates.

Now I'm working through placement of crates, barrels, and a weapon rack, adjusting depths and rotations so the rack doesn't get visually hidden behind the crates and faces the right direction.

I'll scatter bones, coins, and stone chunks on the floor, then add a chained manacle hanging from a ring on the pillar with alternating link rotations, plus a web in the corner. For the pillar itself I'm building it from a stone base, shaft, and cap, with uneven broken chunks on top to suggest damage, sized against a 0.32m brick tile unit.

Now I'm checking texel sizing against the pillar faces to keep bricks looking right, then moving to the sack prop: a squashed sphere shape painted with a mottled noise-based color pattern, plus a tied neck and rope detail.

With the sack done, I'm building the table—plank top, four legs, apron—and planning the tabletop clutter: a candle holder with a glowing flame and wax drip, a stack of books rendered as flat-colored boxes with cream page edges, and a row of bottles.

Adding more props now: glowing potion bottles in green/purple/red with corks, a mug with a torus handle, a rotated cylinder scroll, and a dagger instead of a skull, skipping the map for simplicity. Then I move to the chest—a plank base box with an extruded lid, iron corner straps, a gold lock plate with a dark keyhole, and an arched lid outline built from a series of points.

Setting up a wood paint helper that picks colors with noise variation and darker stripe lines for plank texture, to reuse across the chest lid and straps with a slightly larger scale extrusion.

I'm adding iron straps on the chest sides, spilled gold coins and gems scattered near the front of the chest, then starting a weapon rack with posts, feet, and crossbars.

For the weapons, I'm rethinking the layout as a standing rack with a base platform instead of hanging pieces, placing a sword leaning upright with blade, guard, grip, and pommel positioned from the base up to about shoulder height.

Now I'm adding more rack pieces: an axe with a tall haft and head, a spear with a long shaft and spike tip, and considering a round shield leaning against the front of the rack with a small boss detail, adjusting its position and rotation to make it look propped naturally.

Adding shield emblem texture...

Now I'm designing the skull geometry — a small cranium box with a jawbone piece below, and planning a pixel stamp pattern for the bone texture with dark eye sockets on the front face.

Working out jaw placement relative to the cranium so it sits flush against the skull bottom without floating, then moving on to building bone shapes—thin rods with knobbed ends lying flat on the ground.

Now I'm designing a hanging chain for the pillar: a staple anchor embedded in the stone face, followed by a sequence of alternating links (rotated 90° to show proper linkage) leading down to an iron cuff, positioning everything at the correct depth against the pillar's front surface.

For a small decorative touch, I'm generating a spider web texture on a tiny plane placed in the upper front corner of the pillar, drawing radial strands from the corner outward using a pixelated canvas texture, then mirroring a second plane for a back-to-back effect.

I'm also adding scattered rubble chunks around the pillar base as small randomly rotated stone-colored boxes, sized between 0.1 and 0.2 units, positioned so they rest on the floor.

I'm skipping hanging lanterns since those aren't allowed, but considering small details like a candle skull, gold coins on the chest and table, and a dagger stuck into a crate. I'm laying out a trio of stacked crates near each other with varied rotations and a shared size parameter so the body boxes scale consistently.

Still writing crate geometry...

I'm working out stave placement around the barrel using angle-based hashing, then setting up the lathe-based part builder with its paint and segment parameters. I'm now mapping out the rack and table builders, double-checking which utility imports (noise, pick, snapColor, bayer, cellPaint, skinLayout, skinBox) are actually used versus unused to avoid TypeScript strictness errors.

Writing texture helpers...

I'm sketching the iron tile with darker base and lighter rivets, deciding to skip floor and book textures in favor of flat colors, and planning a modest ~25-color palette to stay under the 64-color limit before writing the brazier code.

Still defining the brazier's legs...

Now I'm adding the ring brace as a thin lathed ring connecting the legs, then placing glowing orange/red coal boxes near the top and flame planes above them for the fire effect.

For the flames I'm using back-to-back planes at different rotations (0, 90, 180, 270 degrees) sized and positioned to cross through the coal area, keeping them glowing so the texture colors pop. I'm also adding a couple wood log rods resting in the bowl near the coals for visual detail.

Now I'm building a weapon rack using a helper function for positioning and rotation, constructing the base plank, side posts, and horizontal bars at set heights and depths to form the rack frame.

Next I'm placing a sword prop leaning against the rack: a steel blade box positioned with careful y-offsets, plus a small rotated diamond-shaped box at the tip to fake a pointed end.

Continuing the sword, I'm adding a dark fuller line down the blade, a gold-colored guard box, a brown cylindrical grip, and a sphere pommel, checking that the hilt doesn't clip through the bar. Now I'm starting the axe prop next to it, building a brown wooden haft rod.

Adding a pole spike and steel coloring for the axe, then placing the spear with a wooden shaft, steel spike head, and red tassel, followed by positioning the shield and sword on the rack at spaced-out x locations.

For the leaning shield disc, I need to orient its cylinder axis to face outward properly using a direction vector rather than fighting with Euler rotation order, so I'll use the `dir` parameter to aim the shield's facing axis toward the viewer with a slight upward lean.

I'm layering the shield: an iron backing disc, a wood disc slightly in front, and the circular texture plane offset further along the normal, with a boss sphere flattened near the center. For the texture itself, I'm designing a quartered red-and-cream pattern with gold cross-lines through the middle to give it a classic heraldic look.

Now I'm placing a table beside the shield — a plank top with four legs, front/back/side aprons for support, and positioning candle holders and a flickering flame prop on its surface.

For the books, I'm stacking them off to the side: a colored cover box for the main shape, then a slightly smaller cream box recessed inward to suggest visible page edges, trying to get the proportions right so pages peek out convincingly rather than poking through the covers.

Book 2 I'm tilting about 20° and coloring blue, book 3 green, skipping the clasp detail for simplicity. Then I move on to the bottles — three cylinders with narrow necks and corks, starting with a green one.

Now I'm adding a mug with a clay-brown body and a torus handle on the side, plus a scroll made from a thin cylinder rotated to lie on its side near one corner of the scene.

Scattering coins, a dagger box, and tied sacks on the table — placing a larger sack to the left with a smaller one nearby, each given a cone-shaped neck and a rope torus wrapped around it for detail.

I'm placing the chest off-center with a slight rotation, then scattering skull-and-bone piles and loose coins near its front. For the barrels, I'm checking distances so they don't overlap with the brazier or chest, nudging positions until each stays clear by enough margin.

Now I'm adjusting the sack positions since one clips the chest's footprint, shifting the chest slightly and repositioning both sacks so they sit just clear of the table's edge, and finalizing the skull pile and brazier coordinates.

For the barrels, I'm varying them for visual interest: one keeps a closed lid, one tips over (skipped for now), and one stays open revealing a glowing toxic-green liquid inside using a dark inner cylinder disc. Writing barrel profile points...

Writing barrel paint logic...

I should also add rubble tiles near the pillar, a bone scatter, and maybe a stray coin pile, then finalize with a meta export block and start on the skull function.

Building the skull geometry and bone texture...

Adding more geometry helpers...
